message:
test(client): make the UI check discriminate, and pin what it checks

`disabled === false` is not pressable. A button can be enabled and off-screen,
transparent, or underneath something else, so the check now asks about layout, the
computed style, the viewport, what elementFromPoint returns at its centre, and
whether it can take focus. Three negative controls run in one script and have to
fail: hidden gives "not laid out", a transparent cover gives "covered by blocker",
and removing each obstruction gives "pressable" again. A fourth loads a page with no
update button -- the shape 0.2.115 shipped -- and that fails too, which is this
file proving it would have caught the release it did not exist for.

The page under test is pinned to the sha256 the signed manifest names, read through
the product's own load_manifest with the operational key compiled in. A manifest that
does not verify does not get to say what the page should be. Same commit and same
toolchain do not make two builds identical; the hash is the only fixed point.

Evidence is graded in the header: the page posting a WebMessage is not evidence that
the native side acted, nor that an updater ran.

Two defects here were mine, in the harness rather than the product. Both eval() and
write_screenshot() captured locals by reference in their completion handlers, so a
late callback wrote through a frame that had gone -- every crash in this file's
history landed after the screenshot, which was the clue. And calling eval() twice
inside one expression re-enters the message loop from both halves of an argument
list; the five pump predicates that called eval are flattened into wait_for(). Four
consecutive runs pass where three used to crash twice.

Not published. The user's install comes first and 0.2.116 stays as it is.
